newsitem.title: INDIA: Trains collide on Bombay rail network, no casualty.
newsitem.headline: Trains collide on Bombay rail network, no casualty.

text.p: Two trains on the suburban Central Railway network in India's commercial capital of Bombay were involved in a small collision on Monday, but no casualties were reported, officials said.
"A local train and a long-distance train had a side collision at 11.37 this morning," a railway spokesman told Reuters. "We have received no reports of any casualties so far."
The incident occurred near the Masjid Bunder railway station, less than one km away from Bombay's main Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, eyewitnesses said.

One side of the motorman's cabin of the local train was crushed under the impact, they said. Two carriages of the long-distance train, the Konarak Express, were partially derailed, and tilted out of position.
Both trains were travelling in the same direction at the time of the crash, railway officials said.
